This Week in the Bay

Tuesday–Sunday, October 6 – 11, 2026 · SF · East Bay · South Bay · North Bay

An unusually loaded week at the strange end of the calendar. Other Minds turns 30 with four nights of premieres at Brava, and the Dutch sound-poet Jaap Blonk plays three different rooms around it — a Mission cinema, a Berkeley living room, an Oakland warehouse — before closing the festival alongside Charlemagne Palestine. A derelict 500-foot crane at Hunters Point becomes a projected monument for two free nights. Litquake opens Thursday, which makes this the biggest literary weekend of the Bay Area year. Chabot opens a new permanent astrophotography gallery and runs its 1883 refractor the same weekend. King Lear closes at Z Space with a live Paul Dresher score; Berkeley Rep’s The Cook closes too. Audium opens a new programme for 176 speakers in total darkness, a vampire hotel opens in North Beach, and a Beijing circus pitches a tent in Oakland. It is also Indigenous Peoples’ Day weekend and Fleet Week, so the waterfront will be chaos from Friday. Filter by day and by region.

🎹 Other Minds 30 · Thu–Sun 📚 Litquake opens Thursday 💡 CRANE at Hunters Point, free 🌌 Chabot’s Shared Sky opens 🎥 Mill Valley Film Fest closes Sun 🧥 Indigenous Peoples’ Day weekend ✈ Fleet Week — expect waterfront traffic

Top 5 This Week

The five best things happening between Tuesday and Sunday, across every category.
  1. Other Minds Festival 30Thu 8 – Sun 11 · Brava Theater, Mission, SFFour nights, five world premieres and the 30th edition of the Bay Area’s flagship new-music festival. Sunday’s finale has Charlemagne Palestine, who almost never plays the US, extending Strumming Music on solo piano.
  2. CRANE: a temporary monument in 5 movementsFri 9 & Sat 10, 5:30–10pm · Hunters Point Shipyard, Bayview, SF · FREEA derelict 500-foot gantry crane wrapped in projected video and a score built from shipyard archives and community voices. Forty minutes, four nights total, free, and nothing like it will happen again.
  3. King Lear, with a live score by Paul DresherThu–Sat 7pm, Sun 2pm · Z Space, Mission, SFThirty-person cast, Rinde Eckert as the Fool, and the Dresher·Davel Invented Instrument Duo playing an original score live. It closes Sunday.
  4. Shared Sky Festival at ChabotSat 10 & Sun 11, 11am–4:30pm · Chabot Space & Science Center, OaklandThe grand opening of a new permanent astrophotography gallery plus the 2026 Astrophotography Prize. Come back after dark for the free 1883 and 1916 refractors on the observatory deck.
  5. Hernan Diaz: Ply, with Ed YongFri 9, 7pm · BATS Improv, Fort Mason, SF · $15Litquake’s opening weekend, and its best pairing: the Pulitzer winner for Trust on his new technology novel, interviewed by the Pulitzer-winning science writer behind An Immense World.

Oddities & One-Offs

13 listings

The favourite lane: small, strange and mostly only-this-weekend. This week it is unusually loaded — a 30th-anniversary new-music festival, a Dutch sound-poet playing three different rooms, a 500-foot crane turned into a monument, and a Halloween oddities market.

🎹
TOP PICK★ SF Classical Voice✦ Palestine rarely plays the US
Oddities & One-Offs · #1Sun 3pm panel · 4pm

Other Minds 30 — Finale: Charlemagne Palestine

Brava Theater, 2781 24th St, Mission
San Francisco
$23–$66

The single best thing happening this week. The 79-year-old sovereign of embodied minimalism — cognac, stuffed animals, overtone saturation — extends his early-1970s Strumming Music on solo piano. Preceded by Jaap Blonk’s sound poetry and Charles Amirkhanian’s Sonatina for Four Bass Drums (1963). Palestine almost never plays the US.

★ SF Classical Voice✦ Five world premieres
Oddities & One-Offs · #2Thu, Fri & Sat · 7pm panel, 8pm concert

Other Minds 30 — Nights 1–3

Brava Theater, 2781 24th St, Mission
San Francisco
$23–$66

Thursday is the world premiere of Joseph Bohigian’s evening-length work on the Soviet-Armenian filmmaker Sergei Parajanov — 18th-century Sayat-Nova bard songs in Armenian, Azeri and Georgian, with duduk, live electronics and video. Friday brings Sylvie Courvoisier solo, Mahsa Vahdat singing Persian poetry in exile, and the world premiere of Juri Seo’s Bad Decision. Saturday has two Kristin Norderval world premieres for voice and electronics with Hardanger fiddle, plus King Britt’s Moksha Black.

Free Telescope Viewings at Chabot

Chabot Observatory Deck, 10000 Skyline Blvd, Oakland
East Bay
FREE

The largest regularly-free public observatory complex in the western US, 1,500 feet above the Bay: Leah (an 8-inch Alvan Clark from 1883), Rachel (a 20-inch refractor from 1916, the biggest publicly accessible refractor in the West) and Nellie, a 36-inch reflector. Clear skies only — check the status page before driving up.

Big Museums

9 listings

Thursday Oct 8 is a monster after-hours night — Exploratorium, Cal Academy, The Tech, the Asian and SFMOMA all run evening programming at once. Note: the de Young’s Late Night Editions do not fall in this window (next is Oct 30), and the Legion of Honor is closed Tue–Thu.

The grand opening of a brand-new permanent gallery, Shared Sky: Photos of Our Universe, with the 2026 Astrophotography Prize winners announced alongside it. Classical, Jazz & Opera

9 listings

SF Opera and SF Ballet are both dark this window. The centre of gravity is Davies on the weekend, the Tákacs Quartet in Berkeley on Sunday, and a deep bench of small rooms — a ragtime quartet in Piedmont, opera in a piano bar, and American Bach Soloists opening their season in three different churches on three nights.

Tákacs Quartet with Jeremy Denk, piano

Zellerbach Hall, UC Berkeley
East Bay

Mendelssohn’s F-minor Op. 80 — the quartet he wrote after his sister died — then a Gabriela Lena Frank piece on Don Quixote’s delusions, then the Franck Piano Quintet with Denk. The Tákacs’ first Bay Area appearance with new cellist Mihai Marica. About as good as chamber music gets.

How this was built

Every source row in sources.md was scanned with the reader its own row specifies — plain fetch, Bright Data Web Unlocker, a documented JSON endpoint, or a full remote browser for the six sources that need one. Fifteen parallel sweeps, one per category, then a single editorial pass to filter, verify and rank. Times were read off each venue’s own event page rather than an aggregator grid wherever one existed.

Double-check before you go

ReOrient Festival had not published per-date curtain times at build time — call Potrero Stage on 415-992-6677. Dracula at TheatreWorks: only Thursday’s 7:30pm is confirmed; the other times follow the venue’s usual pattern. BATS Improv does not publish a curtain time for Saturday. Min Jin Lee, Dorothy Lazard at Clio’s, and all three Marsh shows are sold out with waitlists. LAFS & SLAMS shows conflicting ticketing signals — confirm with the organiser. Telescope nights at Chabot and Foothill are clear-sky only. Nightfall at Filoli is dark on Thursday Oct 8, and Audium has no Thursday show — the new run starts Friday.

Deliberately left out

EDM and DJ club nights, arena concerts, sports, bar crawls, brunch-as-event, networking mixers and sales expos, per the standing anti-preferences. Pride- and identity-framed programming was deprioritised rather than banned — a handful of otherwise on-taste shows this week (Big Gay Halloween at the Great Star, SQREAM at Oasis, the Literary Speakeasy, the Sarah Bush park piece) were held back on that basis. Fleet Week’s air show is noted as context rather than recommended. The Oddities & Curiosities Expo is a standing exclusion.

Sources that came back empty or broken this week

CounterPulse’s October calendar is genuinely blank. ODC, Old First Concerts, Magic Theatre, Central Works, Nerd Nite, Long Now, Music@Menlo, West Edge Opera, LINES Ballet and SF Opera all have nothing inside the window. Walden Pond, Moe’s, Marcus Books and Nomadic Press were live but empty. The Bach Dancing & Dynamite ticketing token has expired and needs re-grabbing. SF Symphony’s calendar is still behind a Cloudflare waiting room — its listings here came from the official season-calendar PDF instead.

88 listings · built for andrew@antimatter.io · the whole Bay Area · Tuesday–Sunday, October 6 – 11, 2026
